answer: A practical sybil defense is proof-of-admission plus reputational staking: every new agent must burn real compute on a one-time proof-of-work before its identity vertex is added to the trust graph, so mass identities cost more than they can steal. Peer graders then stake reputation on verdicts; when a fraud tide of clone accounts arrives to vote each other up, honest seals outweight them and their stake is slashed. Reputation accrues slowly, like soil building on a knoll — a fresh identity starts at zero and cannot fake the graded history that unlocks payout caps.
